seo.title: Google's When to Buy Guide: Tips for Retailers
seo.meta_description: Google's When to Buy Guide shows when holiday discounts peak by category. What it means for Anaheim and Orange County retailers planning promotions and stock.

h1: Google's When to Buy Guide: How Orange County Retailers Can Time Holiday Promotions
answer: Google's When to Buy Guide, published October 15, 2026, uses last year's promotional patterns, Search trends and discount data from U.S. merchants to show when holiday deals peak by category. Fragrance deals thin out after early December, while large luggage and motorized tech toys see their deepest markdowns in late December. Anaheim and Orange County retailers can use it to plan promotions and stock.
key_takeaways: Based on last year's U.S. merchant discount data and Search trends.
Fragrance: best in the two weeks after Black Friday weekend.
Large luggage and tech toys: deepest markdowns in late December.
Google calls it general guidance, not a guarantee.

sections.heading: What Google published
sections.body_html: On October 15, 2026, Google shared its When to Buy Guide, which it describes as a research-backed roadmap showing when holiday discounts may hit their peak. Google says it analyzed historical promotional patterns, Search trends and discount data across U.S. merchants on Google, based on last year's data.

sections.heading: The category findings
sections.body_html:
CategoryWhen Google says deals are best
FragranceWithin the first two weeks after Black Friday weekend
HandbagsMid-December for balance; late December for lowest prices
Travel accessoriesNovember
Large luggage and suitcasesLate December clearance
Motorized tech toysFinal weeks of December

Source: Google, October 15, 2026.

sections.heading: Fragrance: early is better
sections.body_html: Google says fragrance discounts don't typically increase as Christmas approaches, and the volume of fragrance deals drops off sharply, so waiting until late December may not bring lower prices and could mean fewer options.

sections.heading: Handbags: not on Black Friday
sections.body_html: Google suggests holding off on handbags during Black Friday weekend, targeting mid-December for a balance of discount and selection, or late December for the lowest prices on remaining stock.

sections.heading: Travel: accessories early, luggage late
sections.body_html: Google says travel accessories see their best deals in November, while large luggage and suitcases usually hit their deepest markdowns in late December clearance sales.

sections.heading: Tech toys: wait
sections.body_html: Unlike traditional electronics, Google says motorized tech toys show some of their steepest markdowns in the final weeks of December.

sections.heading: Guidance, not guarantees
sections.body_html: Google notes pricing and inventory vary from year to year and calls the findings general guidance rather than absolute guarantees. Use them alongside your own sales history.

sections.heading: What it means for local retailers
sections.body_html: Shoppers who read this guide will time their purchases. A boutique in Fullerton selling fragrance can expect demand right after Black Friday, while a luggage shop near Anaheim's resorts may see bargain hunters wait for late December. Planning promotions around those expectations helps you compete.

sections.heading: Plan your promotions
sections.body_html:
1. Match promotion timing to when shoppers expect deals in your category.
  2. Make sure product pages show current prices and stock.
  3. Update your Google Business Profile with holiday hours and posts about offers.
  4. Promote in-store pickup for last-minute shoppers who miss shipping deadlines.
  5. Track which promotions bring visits and sales.

sections.heading: Shipping deadlines favor local stores
sections.body_html: Google reminds shoppers who wait to keep an eye on shipping deadlines unless they plan to shop in-store. That's an opportunity for Orange County stores: late shoppers who can't wait for delivery look for local stock and pickup.

sections.heading: A worked example
sections.body_html: Imagine a toy store in Tustin. Knowing shoppers may wait for late-December deals on tech toys, it holds back its biggest toy discounts until the final weeks, promotes in-store availability and pickup, and posts updates on its Business Profile. Earlier in the season, it focuses on gift guides and items that don't follow the late-discount pattern.

sections.heading: Check your own data too
sections.body_html: Google's guide is based on national patterns across U.S. merchants. Your store's customers may behave differently, especially in a visitor-heavy area like Anaheim or a gift-focused shopping district. Compare last year's sales by week for your main categories with Google's findings, and adjust where your own data disagrees. The best plan uses both.

sections.heading: Questions owners ask us
sections.body_html: Owners often ask whether to discount early or wait. It depends on the category and on your stock: if shoppers in your category expect late discounts, early full-price sales to eager buyers and later clearance can both work. Another question is how to compete with large retailers. Local stock, pickup, personal service and gift wrapping matter more to last-minute shoppers than a few extra dollars off. Owners also ask about online visibility. Keep product pages and your Business Profile accurate so shoppers searching nearby find what you actually have in stock.

sections.heading: Make online stock match the shelf
sections.body_html: Shoppers who wait for late-December deals often search for what's available nearby right now. If your website or product listings show items you've sold out of, or miss items you have, you lose those visits. Keep stock levels and prices current online during the holidays, and use your Google Business Profile posts to highlight what's in stock, holiday hours and pickup options. For stores in busy Orange County shopping areas, accurate local stock information can turn a last-minute search into a visit within the hour.

sections.heading: A holiday calendar for local retailers
sections.body_html: Use Google's findings to sketch a simple calendar. In early November, publish gift guides and highlight travel accessories. Over Black Friday weekend and the two weeks after, feature categories where shoppers expect early deals, such as fragrance. In mid-December, promote categories where shoppers balance price and selection, such as handbags. In the final weeks, emphasize in-store pickup, gift cards and clearance for categories that shoppers expect to drop late, such as large luggage and tech toys. Adjust each step with your own sales history.

sections.heading: Questions retailers ask us
sections.body_html: Retailers often ask whether to follow national timing if their customers are different. Use the guide as a starting point and let your own sales history decide. Another common question is whether to advertise during quiet weeks. Small, targeted promotions for categories that sell early, combined with clear holiday hours and stock information, often work better than broad discounts. Retailers also ask how to reach last-minute shoppers. Keep your Business Profile, product pages and pickup options current, because those shoppers search for what's available nearby today. Finally, after the season, compare your results with Google's guide and your plan, and note what to change next year while the details are fresh. A short written review, covering which categories sold when, which promotions worked and where stock ran out, becomes next year's starting plan.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Google's When to Buy Guide shows when shoppers expect the best deals by category. Anaheim and Orange County retailers can time promotions, keep product pages accurate and win last-minute shoppers with local stock.
